unmapped_findings: When the strain rate was transiently increased from 0.01 s^-1 to 0.1 s^-1 at ε_I=0.2 (950 °C), the experimental stress gradually reached a lower peak than under the constant 0.1 s^-1 condition; as deformation continued the flow curve exhibited a significant decrease and the steady-state stress was lower than the corresponding constant condition. The greater the strain at which the strain rate transiently increased, the lower the peak and steady-state stress in the second stage.

For this sample (ε_I=0.2), the AGS in the second stage was slightly higher than that under the constant 0.1 s^-1 condition at 0.9 strain; the GOS maps indicate DRX fractions exceeded 94% under constant and increasing strain rates, indicating near-complete recrystallization.

After transiently increasing strain rate at 0.2 strain, the stress softening in the initial part of the second stage was mostly attributed to refinement of the matrix by DRX grains (consistent with the reason for stress decline under constant deformation conditions); the 3D CA model captured the peak stress and subsequent stress decline better than Model 2.

The 3D CA simulation (Fig. 23a) shows that for the transient strain-rate increase at ε_I=0.2, second-stage DRX grains first nucleate at matrix grain boundaries at 0.4 strain, and later (0.6 strain) begin to refine the first-stage DRX grains, consistent with the two-population DRX evolution of this sample.

Per the conclusions, a transient increase in Z_P significantly increases the final AGS with rising ε_I; DRXGs_I cannot be refined completely because of delayed DRXGs_II nucleation, and more/larger DRXGs_I remain as ε_I increases (Table 6 gives the simulated values for this sample).
